column2: Which annotation is used to indicate that a method parameter should be bound to a web request parameter?
column8: @RequestParam is used to bind method parameters to web request parameters.

column4: Annotation is retained in class files
column8: SOURCE retention means the annotation is discarded by the compiler and not retained in class files.

column2: Which ElementType allows an annotation to be applied to method parameters?
column8: ElementType.PARAMETER allows annotations to be applied to method parameters.

column2: What is the default retention policy for annotations in Java?
column8: The default retention policy is CLASS if no @Retention annotation is specified.

column2: What happens when you try to create a custom annotation that validates method return types at runtime?
column8: The answer depends on how you implement the validation using reflection and when you check the annotations.

column2: How would you implement a custom annotation processor that generates code at compile time for dependency injection patterns?
column8: Custom annotation processors extend AbstractProcessor and use @SupportedAnnotationTypes to process annotations at compile time.
